analysis: The closest option covers the programme-wide mix of rhetoric, media use and effects, persuasion, politics and empirical inquiry. Film & Media, From T.V. to TikTok, Media & Race and The Documentary give substantive media coverage. Research Methods & Statistics, Statistics & Experimental Methods and Qualitative Research Methodology develop survey, experiment and qualitative skills. Advanced Research Methods & Statistics adds evidence synthesis in place of a weak thematic elective, with Brain & Behavior meeting its formal prerequisite. Organisational psychology and marketing add the corporate and audience perspectives.

The second option has a sustained marketing and communication sequence through consumer design, marketing strategy, market research, digital transformation and persuasion. Behavioural economics and social psychology give audience decision theory. Medical & Health Psychology and Epidemiology supply the health context. Generic biomedical disease and immunology courses were removed because they did not develop audience, message or behaviour research. This is health behaviour within persuasive communication, without claiming the breadth of a dedicated health communication curriculum.

The third option puts public institutions, public policy, rights, civil society and trust alongside political rhetoric and media representations. Documentary production offers non-fiction media practice and ethical choices, while political methods, public-policy writing and qualitative research support inquiry into public debate. This is a media and political communication programme with relevant documentary practice. UvA still gives more dedicated study to news production roles, audiences and the relationship between journalism and democracy.

The three alternatives differ by 52.5, 52.5 and 90 EC each way. Their advanced work distinguishes media and representation, organisational and consumer behaviour, and public institutions and documentary practice. The strongest comparison remains the broad option. Entertainment and intercultural themes were considered; entertainment has substantial coverage in the closest option and the intercultural topic does not change the Dutch programme target. The three-option limit applies.
constructionStop: Three academically viable and distinct compositions meet the maximum.

alignment.rationale: Both study how messages influence people. UCR applies persuasion techniques in a community project.
Both study entertainment media and how audiences engage with them. UCR examines representation and cultural history.
UCR courses address rhetoric, media and social behaviour separately. UvA introduces communication science across these areas.
UCR media courses examine technologies, representation and history. UvA focuses on media industries, markets and regulation.
UCR addresses digital strategy, but the selected courses do not dedicate a course to AI in strategic communication.
UCR studies persuasion and digital media in separate courses. UvA applies communication research to algorithmic targeting and influence.
Both use evidence to develop practical recommendations. UCR focuses on marketing and consumer engagement.
Both develop survey design, measurement and data analysis through a practical research project.
Both examine relationships inside organisations. UvA also studies how organisations communicate with external stakeholders.
Both teach qualitative research design and interpretation through social research.
UCR combines politics, rhetoric and documentary practice. UvA studies how news media, journalists, audiences and politics interact.
Both develop experimental design and analysis. UCR applies them to health and behaviour, while UvA studies communication effects.
Both support academic skills and reflection. UvA’s tutor and portfolio activities run through the first three semesters.
UCR research methods and statistics are used in separate comparisons with the survey and experiment courses.
Some UCR courses examine evidence and ethical reasoning. UvA gives philosophy of science and methodology dedicated attention.
UCR media analysis and data science offer related skills. UvA requires practical quantitative media content analysis.
UCR advanced research methods focuses on meta-analysis. UvA teaches statistical reasoning across communication research.
Some UCR courses include projects with external partners. UvA requires a separate supervised internship with research.
This is approved open elective space.
UvA requires a graduation project and individual thesis. UCR’s independent research element is optional.
